# Files that own a format written to disk and read back by a LATER agent.
#
# Touching one of these makes a pull request answer a compatibility
# question before it can merge (.github/scripts/compat_gate.py, a copy of
# TimeLakeDB's; timelakedb#173). The list is deliberately explicit rather
# than a pattern: "anything with a serde derive" would catch every config
# struct and the gate would be noise inside a week.
#
# This file is itself on the list, by the entry below. Adding a new
# persisted format therefore trips the gate on the commit that adds it,
# which is the one commit where somebody still remembers how it is meant to
# be read by the next version.
#
# What an agent upgrade has to survive: the checkpoint (where every source
# was, and the stamper state that makes a replay reproduce identical
# timestamps rather than collide) and the spool (batches read off a source
# and not yet acknowledged by the database, which is the only copy of those
# lines anywhere). The spool directory NAMES are a format too — an agent
# that looks for its queue under a new name strands the old one, which is
# exactly the loss the queue exists to prevent — so they live in queue.rs
# rather than in main.rs, and queue.rs is watched.
#
# Deliberately not listed: dead-letter-<name>.lp (append-only; read by
# people, never by the agent), the journald cursor and winlog bookmark (opaque
# strings the OS defines, carried INSIDE the checkpoint), config.toml and a
# label_file (operator-authored input, not agent output).
#
# Format = one line, a path, then optional whitespace and a comment.

crates/tributary/src/checkpoint.rs   # <stream>.checkpoint JSON: file marks, stamper state, lateness, cursor; CHECKPOINT_FORMAT_VERSION
crates/tributary/src/queue.rs        # queue-<name>/NNNNNNNNNNNN.lp segments (raw line protocol) and the spool directory names; QUEUE_FORMAT_VERSION
.github/persisted-formats.txt
